# apple-llm: integration guide for AI agents

> Integrate Apple's on-device LLM, text to speech (TTS), and speech to text
> (STT) into a project with Node.js, Python, a CLI, or a local HTTP server.
> No API key or account is needed. Inference requires macOS 26+ on Apple Silicon.

This is the self-contained agent reference for the apple-llm 0.3 API. Read it
before writing an integration. Check the installed package version and runtime
capabilities; features depend on the Mac and macOS release.

- Website: https://jagdishpal02000.github.io/apple-llm/
- Shareable guide: https://jagdishpal02000.github.io/apple-llm/llms.txt
- Raw source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jagdishpal02000/apple-llm/main/llms.txt
- Repository: https://github.com/jagdishpal02000/apple-llm
- npm package: `apple-llm`; imports from `apple-llm`.
- PyPI package: `apple-llm`; imports from `apple_llm`.

## How to use this file

Give an agent the guide URL, attach this file, or paste its contents into the
agent's project context. Example request:

"Read https://jagdishpal02000.github.io/apple-llm/llms.txt and integrate
apple-llm into this project for local LLM, TTS, and STT. Use the existing
language and architecture, keep processing on device, check availability,
and include setup instructions and a smoke test."

This URL supplies documentation. It is not an MCP server endpoint, and
apple-llm does not currently ship an MCP server or an `mcp` CLI command.
An agent can use the SDK, run the CLI, or call the HTTP API directly. If the
host requires MCP, implement a separate adapter with the host's MCP SDK and
wrap the documented functions as tools; do not register this text URL as an
MCP transport. Suggested mappings: `generate_text` to `llm.text()`,
`synthesize_speech` to `synthesize()`, and `transcribe_audio` to `transcribe()`.
The adapter and apple-llm must execute on a supported Mac.

## Integration workflow

1. Inspect the target project's language, runtime, and existing AI/audio code.
2. Choose the smallest integration: Node SDK, Python SDK, CLI, or HTTP server.
3. Check the machine requirements below. Use the speech probe independently
   of the LLM probe when only TTS/STT is needed.
4. Use `tier: 'device'` / `tier="device"` for a local-only LLM. The SDK default
   `auto` can select cloud when the device is unavailable and cloud is set up.
5. Keep clients alive, provide cleanup, handle typed errors, and surface setup
   failures to the user. Do not silently switch a local-only project to cloud.
6. Verify one short text request, one synthesized file, and one transcription
   as applicable. Microphone capture is a separate, user-initiated feature.

## Requirements and execution location

| Requirement | Local LLM | TTS and STT |
| --- | --- | --- |
| macOS 26+ on Apple Silicon | Required | Required |
| Xcode Command Line Tools (`xcode-select --install`) | Required | Required |
| Apple Intelligence enabled and model ready | Required | Not required |
| Apple account, API key, full Xcode, developer membership | Not required | Not required |
| Internet during normal on-device processing | Not required once assets are installed | Not required once speech language assets are installed |

Node requires Node.js >=18; Python requires Python >=3.10. Both packages have
zero required runtime dependencies. Pydantic, schema libraries, OpenAI clients,
and the Vercel AI SDK are optional integrations installed separately.

Imports and installation work on unsupported platforms; inference does not.
There is no Linux, Windows, Intel Mac, or automatic alternate-model backend.
Run the SDK in a native Mac process, not a Linux container, browser bundle,
edge runtime, or Linux serverless function. Other runtimes can call an HTTP
server running on a supported Mac; `127.0.0.1` always means the caller's host.

Both packages compile a small Swift helper on first use, not at install time.
The cached binary is shared between Node and Python under
`~/Library/Caches/apple-llm/bin/`. Allow time for the first compilation;
`onProgress` / `on_progress` can report progress. Do not depend on `/usr/bin/fm`,
an Ollama installation, a model download from Hugging Face, or a paid license.

## Installation and discovery

Install the binding that matches the project:

```sh
npm install apple-llm
# Python alternative:
python -m pip install apple-llm
```

CLI discovery (the Node executable can run without a global install):

```sh
npx apple-llm probe --json
npx apple-llm voices --json
npx apple-llm languages --json
```

In Python projects, the pip package installs `apple-llm`; use
`apple-llm probe --json`. The HTTP `serve` command is Node-only.

```js
import { probe, probeSpeech } from 'apple-llm';

const models = await probe();
const speech = await probeSpeech();
console.log(models.device.available, models.device.reason);
console.log(speech.available, speech.reason);
```

```python
from apple_llm import probe, probe_speech

models = probe()
speech = probe_speech()
print(models["device"]["available"], models["device"].get("reason"))
print(speech["available"], speech.get("reason"))
```

`probe()` reports `device` and `cloud`, including availability and setup
information. Use the device's `contextSize` and reported capabilities rather
than hardcoding a model's abilities. `probeSpeech()` / `probe_speech()` reports
speech availability, voices, languages, and defaults. An unavailable LLM does
not mean speech is unavailable.

## Node.js / TypeScript: local LLM

The package supports ESM and CommonJS. The following ESM example also works as
an `.mjs` file. Keep one client for the application's lifetime and close it on
shutdown; this example closes it after the requests.

```js
import { AppleLLM } from 'apple-llm';

const llm = new AppleLLM({ tier: 'device', timeoutMs: 30_000 });
try {
  const text = await llm.text('Summarize: The meeting moved to Friday.', {
    system: 'Answer in one short sentence.',
    maxTokens: 128,
  });
  console.log(text);

  const contact = await llm.json('Ada Lovelace was born in 1815.', {
    schema: {
      type: 'object',
      properties: { name: { type: 'string' }, born: { type: 'integer' } },
      required: ['name', 'born'],
      additionalProperties: false,
    },
  });
  console.log(contact);

  for await (const delta of llm.stream('Write a short greeting.')) {
    process.stdout.write(delta);
  }
  process.stdout.write('\n');
} finally {
  llm.close();
}
```

- `text(input, options?)` returns a string.
- `json(input, { schema, ...options })` returns the parsed object. Plain JSON
  Schema works without extra dependencies. Zod 4 / Standard Schema adds typed
  validation; import Zod from a separately installed `zod` package.
- `generate(input, options?)` returns `text`, `object`, `message`, `usage`,
  `finishReason`, `toolCalls`, `tier`, and `trimmedTurns`.
- `stream()` supports async iteration, awaiting the full text, and `.result`
  for metadata. `streamJson()` yields partial objects; validate/use the final
  object before committing downstream changes.
- Input may be a prompt string or a list of `{ role, content }` chat messages.
  Append `result.message` to history; `trimHistory` defaults to true for message
  lists. Use `trimHistory: false` to fail instead of dropping old turns.
- `llm.conversation('thread-id', { system: '...' })` maintains a named device
  conversation; its `.text()` and `.json()` methods continue that thread.
- Options include `system`, `temperature`, `maxTokens`, `timeoutMs`, `signal`,
  `images`, `documents`, `sessionId`, `tools`, `maxToolCalls`, `useCase`,
  `guardrails`, `sampling`, and cloud-only `webSearch`.
- `llm.countTokens(input)` returns `{ tokens, contextSize }` on supported OS
  versions. `llm.prewarm()` loads assets. Do not assume token usage is reported
  on every tier/OS.

### Node function tools

Use custom tools on device. `execute` runs in your application process. This
example uses optional Zod 4 (`npm install zod`) to infer and validate arguments:

```js
import { AppleLLM, tool } from 'apple-llm';
import { z } from 'zod';

const lookupStatus = tool({
  name: 'lookupStatus',
  description: 'Look up the status of a support ticket by ID.',
  parameters: z.object({ id: z.string() }),
  execute: async ({ id }) => ({ id, status: 'open' }),
});
const llm = new AppleLLM({ tier: 'device' });
try {
  const result = await llm.generate('What is the status of ticket A123?', {
    tools: [lookupStatus],
  });
  console.log(result.text, result.toolCalls);
} finally {
  llm.close();
}
```

Replace the example lookup with the project's own data access. Without
`execute`, generation returns pending tool calls with
`finishReason: 'tool-calls'`; execute them in the host and return tool messages
to continue. Built-in tools are `ocr`, `barcode`, and `spotlight`, where the OS
supports them. Generic JavaScript function tools are not Python features.

## Python: local LLM

```python
from apple_llm import AppleLLM

with AppleLLM(tier="device") as llm:
    text = llm.text(
        "Summarize: The meeting moved to Friday.",
        system="Answer in one short sentence.",
        max_tokens=128,
    )
    print(text)
    contact = llm.json("Ada Lovelace was born in 1815.", schema={
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {"name": {"type": "string"}, "born": {"type": "integer"}},
        "required": ["name", "born"],
        "additionalProperties": False,
    })
    print(contact)
    llm.stream("Write a short greeting.", on_delta=lambda s: print(s, end="", flush=True))
    print()
```

Python `stream()` returns the completed string and emits deltas through
`on_delta`; it is not Node's async iterator API. `json()` accepts a dict schema
or a Pydantic v2 `BaseModel` subclass and returns a validated model instance
for the latter. Install the optional extra with
`python -m pip install 'apple-llm[pydantic]'`.

```python
import asyncio
from apple_llm import AsyncAppleLLM

async def main():
    async with AsyncAppleLLM(tier="device") as llm:
        print(await llm.text("Write a short greeting."))

asyncio.run(main())
```

Python uses snake_case options: `max_tokens`, `session_id`, `use_case`,
`web_search`, and `on_progress`. Conversations use
`llm.conversation('thread-id', system='...')`. Images, text documents, built-in
tools, `count_tokens()`, `prewarm()`, and writing helpers are supported. Do not
port Node-only message-list, `generate()`, `streamJson()`, function tool, or
AbortSignal APIs verbatim to Python.

## Text to speech: playback and audio files

`speak()` plays on the Mac running the code. For a browser, remote client, or
download, use `synthesize()` or the HTTP speech endpoint and play the returned
audio in that client.

```js
import { AppleSpeech } from 'apple-llm';

const speech = new AppleSpeech();
try {
  console.log(await speech.voices({ language: 'en', novelty: false }));
  await speech.speak('Hello there');
  const made = await speech.synthesize('Hello there', { format: 'wav' });
  console.log(made.audio.length, made.duration); // Buffer; seconds
  const saved = await speech.synthesize('A longer article.', { out: 'article.m4a' });
  console.log(saved.path); // file result, no audio Buffer
} finally {
  speech.close();
}
```

```python
from apple_llm import AppleSpeech

with AppleSpeech() as speech:
    print(speech.voices(language="en", novelty=False))
    speech.speak("Hello there")
    made = speech.synthesize("Hello there", format="wav")
    print(len(made.audio), made.duration)  # bytes; seconds
    saved = speech.synthesize("A longer article.", out="article.m4a")
    print(saved.path)
```

Convenience exports share a default speech helper: Node `speak`, `synthesize`,
`listVoices`, `systemVoice`; Python `speak`, `synthesize`, `list_voices`,
`system_voice`. Explicit `AppleSpeech` instances give each workload its own
helper and cleanup. Python also has awaitable `AsyncAppleSpeech`.

TTS options: `voice` (installed name/id, or `system`), `language`, `speed`
(1 = normal), `pitch` (0.5–2), `volume` (0–1), and `ssml`. Synthesis adds
`format`, `out`, `words`, and `sampleRate` (Python `sample_rate`). Installed
voices vary: list them before hardcoding a name. Omit `voice` for the System
voice or use `language` to select one. Unknown voices raise `UnsupportedError`.

Output formats: `wav`, `m4a`, `aac`, `flac`, `aiff`, `caf`, `pcm`. The byte
default is WAV; a file's extension selects its format unless overridden.
PCM is raw 16-bit little-endian mono. Parse WAV chunks instead of assuming a
44-byte header. Prefer `out` for long text to avoid holding all audio in memory.
Direct SDK/CLI MP3, Ogg, and Opus encoding is unsupported.

`avspeech` voices support pitch, volume, SSML, and rendered word timings.
`say` voices support speed but not those controls. They can lose words during
concurrent LLM activity, so file synthesis verifies two renders. Siri voices
cannot be selected by name; selecting one as the macOS System voice may work
with `voice: 'system'`, but that path is unverified. Do not promise it.

The package is MIT licensed. System voices are subject to Apple's separate
macOS license; do not infer permission to distribute synthesized audio from
the package license. See the repository's existing voice-license notes:
https://github.com/jagdishpal02000/apple-llm#the-licence-on-voices

## Speech to text: recordings, subtitles, and microphone

```js
import { AppleSpeech, toSRT, toVTT } from 'apple-llm';

const speech = new AppleSpeech();
try {
  const result = await speech.transcribe('meeting.m4a', {
    language: 'en-US',
    words: true,
    hints: ['Kubernetes', 'Postgres'],
  });
  console.log(result.text, result.segments, result.language, result.engine);
  console.log(toSRT(result), toVTT(result));
} finally {
  speech.close();
}
```

```python
from apple_llm import AppleSpeech

with AppleSpeech() as speech:
    result = speech.transcribe(
        "meeting.m4a", language="en-US", words=True,
        hints=["Kubernetes", "Postgres"],
    )
    print(result.text, result.segments, result.language, result.engine)
    print(result.to_srt(), result.to_vtt())
```

Input can be a file path or encoded file bytes; pass `filename` for bytes
whose format is ambiguous. macOS reads WAV, AIFF, CAF, MP3, M4A, AAC, FLAC,
and MP4/MOV video. Convert WebM, Ogg, or MKV first. Browser recordings often
use WebM/Opus: select a supported recording format or convert before upload;
renaming a file does not convert it.

There is no language autodetection. Pass `language`, e.g. `en-US` or `en`;
the default is the Mac's language. Missing recognition assets download on
first use unless `download: false` / `download=False` is set. Available
languages and engines vary by OS. `engine` is `transcriber` or `dictation`.
Language APIs: Node `listSpeechLanguages`, `installSpeechLanguage`,
`removeSpeechLanguage`; Python `list_speech_languages`,
`install_speech_language`, `remove_speech_language`.

Segments include text and start/end seconds. `words: true` / `words=True`
adds word timings/confidence. Node `onSegment` / Python `on_segment` reports
finished segments; `onProgress` / `on_progress` reports operation progress.
Node `transcribeStream()` yields finished segments with async iteration;
it processes an existing recording, not uploaded live audio chunks.

One utterance from the Mac's microphone:

```js
import { listen } from 'apple-llm';
const text = await listen({ language: 'en-US', silence: 1.5, maxSeconds: 30 });
console.log(text); // string, not Transcript
```

```python
from apple_llm import listen_once
result = listen_once(language="en-US", silence=1.5, max_seconds=30)
print(result.text)  # listen_once returns a Transcript
```

For continuous recognition, Node `listen({ continuous: true })` returns a
session that is async iterable over `{ text, final, start, end, ... }` events.
Call `session.stop()` to keep the transcript or `session.abort()` to cancel.
Python `with listen(continuous=True) as session:` is synchronously iterable;
use `session.stop()` or `session.cancel()`. Partial (`final: false`) events
replace the previous guess; do not append every partial to the transcript.
macOS requests microphone access for the launching app; a denial raises
`PermissionDeniedError`. The microphone hears speaker playback too.

## Local voice assistant: STT to LLM to TTS

This runnable Node example handles one spoken question. Use headphones.

```js
import { AppleLLM, AppleSpeech } from 'apple-llm';

const llm = new AppleLLM({ tier: 'device' });
const speech = new AppleSpeech();
try {
  const question = await speech.listen({ language: 'en-US', maxSeconds: 30 });
  if (question.trim()) {
    const answer = await llm.text(question, {
      system: 'Answer in one or two short sentences.', maxTokens: 128,
    });
    await speech.speak(answer);
  }
} finally {
  speech.close();
  llm.close();
}
```

## HTTP integration: OpenAI-compatible server

Start the Node server on the Mac; keep it running while the client connects:

```sh
npx apple-llm serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 11436 --tier device
```

- OpenAI base URL: `http://127.0.0.1:11436/v1`.
- Local model ID: `apple-on-device`.
- Optional cloud model ID: `apple-private-cloud` (requires cloud setup).
- SDK API key: any nonempty value, such as `unused`, unless server
  `--api-key <key>` requires the matching `Authorization: Bearer <key>`.
- `--tier device` chooses the default; an explicit `apple-private-cloud`
  request still selects cloud. Use the local model ID for local requests.
- CORS is off by default; `--cors http://localhost:5173` allows that frontend
  origin. Browser code calls this API, rather than importing the Node SDK.
- To serve another machine, bind an appropriate interface with `--host` and
  configure authentication/network access. Use the Mac's reachable hostname
  from that client. A static website does not host Mac inference.

```sh
curl http://127.0.0.1:11436/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"apple-on-device","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Write a short greeting."}],"max_tokens":128}'

curl http://127.0.0.1:11436/v1/audio/speech \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"tts-1","voice":"alloy","input":"Hello there","response_format":"wav"}' \
  --output hello.wav

curl http://127.0.0.1:11436/v1/audio/transcriptions \
  -F model=whisper-1 -F file=@hello.wav -F language=en -F response_format=json
```

`tts-1` and `whisper-1` are client-compatible labels; audio endpoints ignore
`model` and use macOS speech, not OpenAI's hosted models.

| Endpoint | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /v1/models` | Lists the two model IDs, not proof that either is available |
| `GET /health` or `/v1/health` | LLM availability; can return 503 while speech still works |
| `POST /v1/chat/completions` | Chat, SSE with `stream: true`, tools, images, JSON Schema, `seed`, `top_p` |
| `GET /v1/audio/voices` | `{ object: 'list', data: [...] }` of installed macOS voices |
| `POST /v1/audio/speech` | JSON `input`, optional `voice`, `speed`, `response_format`; binary audio response |
| `POST /v1/audio/transcriptions` | Multipart `file`, optional `language`, `prompt`, `response_format`, `timestamp_granularities[]` |

For constrained chat JSON, send
`response_format: { type: 'json_schema', json_schema: { name: 'Result', schema: ... } }`.
Tool calls are OpenAI-style; the HTTP client runs its own tools and sends tool
messages to continue. No `/v1/responses`, embeddings, hosted assistants,
Realtime/WebSocket speech, audio translation, or HTTP microphone endpoint is
implemented. OpenAI compatibility covers the documented routes.

Audio details matter:

- OpenAI voice aliases (`alloy`, `nova`, etc.) select the Mac's System voice.
  Use a name/id from `/v1/audio/voices` to select an installed voice.
- HTTP speech defaults to AAC, including requests for `mp3` or `opus`, because
  macOS cannot encode those formats. Respect `Content-Type`; do not save AAC
  bytes with an MP3 extension. Request `wav` explicitly for WAV output.
- HTTP speech formats: `wav`, `m4a`, `aac`, `flac`, `aiff`, `pcm`; PCM is
  24 kHz, 16-bit little-endian mono. `caf` is SDK/CLI-only.
- Transcription response formats: `json` (`{ text }`), `text`, `srt`, `vtt`,
  `verbose_json`. Word timestamps use `timestamp_granularities[]=word` with
  `verbose_json`. `prompt` is split on commas/newlines into recognition hints.
- HTTP audio uploads are limited to 512 MiB. SDK/CLI file inputs do not have
  that server upload limit. TTS returns a rendered file, not live audio chunks.

An existing Python OpenAI client can use all three capabilities:

```python
# Optional client dependency: python -m pip install openai
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(base_url="http://127.0.0.1:11436/v1", api_key="unused")
reply = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="apple-on-device", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Say hello."}],
)
print(reply.choices[0].message.content)
audio = client.audio.speech.create(
    model="tts-1", voice="alloy", input="Hello there", response_format="wav",
)
audio.write_to_file("hello.wav")
with open("hello.wav", "rb") as recording:
    print(client.audio.transcriptions.create(
        model="whisper-1", file=recording, language="en",
    ).text)
```

## Ollama-compatible apps and Vercel AI SDK

The same server provides Ollama's API at `http://127.0.0.1:11436` (no `/v1`).
Point an Ollama-compatible app there and select `apple-on-device`. To use
the usual Ollama port, stop any process using it and start
`npx apple-llm serve --port 11434`. No Ollama daemon or model pull is needed.

Supported routes: `/api/chat`, `/api/generate`, `/api/tags`, `/api/show`,
`/api/ps`, `/api/version`. Chat/generate stream NDJSON by default; use
`stream: false` for one response. They accept `format` (`"json"` or JSON
Schema), tools, images, and generation `options` including `temperature`,
`num_predict`, `seed`, `top_p`. Embeddings and model installation are not served.

For Vercel AI SDK 6/7, install `ai` separately and use the Node provider:

```js
import { generateText } from 'ai';
import { apple } from 'apple-llm/ai-sdk';

const { text } = await generateText({
  model: apple(), // on device; apple('cloud') opts into cloud
  prompt: 'Write a short greeting.',
});
console.log(text);
```

The provider supports text/object generation, streaming, tool calls, images,
and abort signals. Apple options go in
`providerOptions: { apple: { useCase, guardrails, builtInTools } }`.

## CLI integration

Use argument arrays when launching commands from application code; do not
interpolate untrusted text into a shell command. For repeated LLM calls,
prefer a persistent SDK client or HTTP server over a CLI process per request.

```sh
npx apple-llm run --tier device "Write a short greeting."
npx apple-llm run --tier device --system "Be concise." -   # prompt on stdin
npx apple-llm run --tier device --schema schema.json "Extract fields."
npx apple-llm run --tier device --stream "Write a short greeting."
npx apple-llm speak "Hello there"                         # Mac speaker playback
npx apple-llm speak --file notes.txt -o notes.m4a          # audio file
npx apple-llm transcribe meeting.mp4 -o meeting.srt        # text/json/srt/vtt by extension
npx apple-llm listen --once                              # microphone
npx apple-llm languages install en-US
npx apple-llm --help
```

Both CLIs provide model/speech commands, schema files, images, built-in tools,
sessions, token counting, and writing presets. Node additionally provides
`serve` and interactive `chat`. `run --json` in Node returns result metadata;
Python does not have every Node flag. Consult the installed CLI's `--help`.

## Optional cloud tier

Cloud sends prompts and supplied attachments to Apple's Private Cloud Compute.
It is not local or offline. Use it only when it matches the user's requirements.
One-time setup generates, signs, and imports a Shortcut on the Mac:

```sh
npx apple-llm setup-cloud
# A separate web-search-enabled Shortcut:
npx apple-llm setup-cloud --web-search
```

Node: `new AppleLLM({ tier: 'cloud', fallback: 'device' })`.
Python: `AppleLLM(tier="cloud", fallback="device")`.
The fallback handles cloud quota/rate-limit failures; it does not make cloud
requests local or guarantee every kind of failure will fall back. In Node,
`generate()` reports the tier that actually answered.

Cloud has roughly a 32,768-token window, returns one chunk, and has no
constrained decoding or callable custom tools through this library. JSON is
requested, recovered, and can fail validation. Node supports cloud images on
compatible macOS 27 releases; Python's high-level client currently rejects
cloud images. `webSearch: true` / `web_search=True` uses the web-enabled Shortcut.
Private Shortcuts behavior can change between OS releases.

Apple imposes a per-Mac quota plus a short-term rate limit. `probe().cloud.quota`
cannot predict the short-term limiter. Catch `QuotaError`, respect a reported
reset time, and back off or use an explicitly configured device fallback.
Do not use cloud for unbounded batch jobs.

## Model limits, structured output, and operation

- Device context is typically 4,096 tokens on macOS 26 and 8,192 on macOS 27;
  inspect the runtime probe. Budget instructions, history, input, schema,
  tools, and output together. Bound input and output; chunk long documents.
- The small on-device model suits classification, extraction, tagging,
  rewriting, summaries, and short answers. Do not rely on it for complex
  reasoning, large code generation, embeddings, or live web knowledge.
- Vision and built-in tools need matching OS capabilities (typically macOS
  27+). Text `documents` are inlined; they are not arbitrary binary/PDF parsing.
  `askScreen` / `ask_screen` captures the Mac screen and needs the appropriate
  macOS screen-capture access.
- Leave the default temperature at `0.4`. Greedy `temperature: 0` can cause
  repetition and severe latency during constrained generation. For repeatable
  Node output use `sampling: { mode: 'topK', k: 50, seed: 42 }`; Python exports
  `sampling_seeded(42)`.
- Device structured output enforces Apple's supported schema shape. Not every
  JSON Schema constraint is enforced: bound arrays with `maxItems`; do not
  rely on string `maxLength` or semantic correctness. Standard Schema/Pydantic
  validation checks additional constraints after generation.
- The SDK translates JSON Schema to Apple's dialect. Do not hand-edit
  `x-order`, titles, enums, `$ref`, unions, or `additionalProperties` to work
  around it. Pass the standard schema to `json()`.
- Reuse clients to keep the helper warm. Apple serializes inference; spawning
  many clients does not increase model throughput. Each helper handles one
  request at a time; use separate `AppleSpeech` instances for independent
  speech workloads. Close clients during shutdown.
- Named conversations persist on disk; use distinct IDs for unrelated users
  and the conversation reset APIs when clearing history.
- Node helpers include `rewrite`, `proofread`, `summarize`, `draft`, `tone`,
  and `askScreen`; Python has `rewrite`, `proofread`, `summarize`, `draft`,
  and `ask_screen`, with snake_case options.
  Long-text `summarize` can split work into parts.

## Errors and troubleshooting

Branch on exported error classes, not substrings of Apple's messages. Node
errors extend `AppleLLMError` and have stable `.code` values; Python errors
also extend `AppleLLMError` but do not share the Node `.code` API.

| Error | Integration response |
| --- | --- |
| `ModelUnavailableError` | Read `.reason`: unsupported platform/OS, ineligible device, disabled Apple Intelligence, model not ready, or missing compiler; show the relevant setup action |
| `SetupRequiredError` | Complete the named setup step: cloud Shortcut or recognition language assets |
| `UnsupportedError` | Change an unsupported format, voice, language, OS feature, or tier option; do not silently substitute |
| `PermissionDeniedError` | Explain the microphone permission for the launching app in macOS Settings |
| `ContextLengthError` | Reduce input/history/schema/output budget or chunk work |
| `SchemaRejectedError` | Simplify the schema or check dialect support |
| `SchemaValidationError` | Handle invalid structured output; Node exposes `.issues`/`.text`, Python exposes the failed text where available |
| `QuotaError` | Back off; Node `.resetDate`, Python `.reset_date` when available; optional device fallback |
| `TimeoutError` | Surface the timeout and allow retry; explicitly import Python's error to distinguish it from the builtin |
| `AbortError` (Node), `CancelledError` (Python) | Treat user cancellation as expected |
| `RefusalError` | Surface the model's refusal |
| `ToolExecutionError`, `ModelBusyError` (Node) | Inspect the tool failure or exhausted busy-model retries |

Troubleshooting order: check OS/architecture, run the appropriate probe,
verify `xcode-select --install`, check Apple Intelligence only for LLM use,
list available voices/languages for speech, then reproduce with one short
request. Do not diagnose speech failure from `/health` alone. A successful
`/v1/models` call proves discovery works, not that a model is ready.

## Verification and maintenance

For an integration, check: device-only model selection, successful text output,
valid structured fields, nonempty correctly formatted audio, transcription of
a known recording, cleanup, and an understandable unavailable/setup path.
Test microphone capture interactively when that feature is requested. Avoid
cloud calls in routine smoke tests because they send data off-device and
consume quota. Runtime probes are more reliable than OS/model-name assumptions.

For maintainers: this root `llms.txt` is the single source for the agent guide.
The website serves it during development and emits the same bytes at build
time; do not maintain a second hand-written copy. Update it when public APIs,
requirements, or supported routes change. Check these implementation sources
if a package version differs from this guide:

- Node API: https://github.com/jagdishpal02000/apple-llm/blob/main/packages/node/README.md
- Python API: https://github.com/jagdishpal02000/apple-llm/blob/main/packages/python/README.md
- Node exports/types: https://github.com/jagdishpal02000/apple-llm/blob/main/packages/node/src/index.ts
- Node LLM client: https://github.com/jagdishpal02000/apple-llm/blob/main/packages/node/src/client.ts
- Speech types/client: https://github.com/jagdishpal02000/apple-llm/blob/main/packages/node/src/speech.ts
- HTTP routes: https://github.com/jagdishpal02000/apple-llm/blob/main/packages/node/src/server.ts
- Python LLM client: https://github.com/jagdishpal02000/apple-llm/blob/main/packages/python/src/apple_llm/__init__.py
- Python speech: https://github.com/jagdishpal02000/apple-llm/blob/main/packages/python/src/apple_llm/_speech.py
- Examples: https://github.com/jagdishpal02000/apple-llm/tree/main/packages/node/examples
- Changelog: https://github.com/jagdishpal02000/apple-llm/blob/main/packages/node/CHANGELOG.md

Repository checks: run `npm test` and `npm run typecheck` in `packages/node`,
`pytest` in `packages/python`, and `npm run build` in `site`. Hardware tests
are opt-in with `APPLE_LLM_LIVE=1`; cloud tests additionally need
`APPLE_LLM_LIVE_CLOUD=1` and a configured Shortcut. The shared Swift source is
`swift/helper.swift`; `scripts/embed-helper.mjs` synchronizes package copies.
